CIVIL REVISION NO 114 OF 1988 (Syllaet)
CIVIL REVISION NO. 4873 OF 1991 (Dhaka)
lawyer:
Mr. J.N. Dev for the Petitioner 
Mr. H.N. Nandi with Mr. T. K. Dutta for the opposite party

Md. Rajiuddin Chowdhury ------ petitioner
VERSUS
Suruj Ali ------ Opposite party
full_judgment:
ABU SAYEED AHAMED, J: Present Rule at the instance of plaintiff against the judgment of affirmance in a suit for possession on redemption of mortgage. Plaintiff Md. Rajiuddin Chowdhury transferred 54 acres agricultural land for Tk. 700/- to the defendant Suruj Ali, by kabala executed on 10.7.49 (Ext.1). Transferee executed an Ekrarnama on 13.7.49 (Ext.2). Both the documents were registered on 7.11.49. Transferee agreed to recovery the land as per terms of ekrarnama if consideration money was paid back within 6 years. After promulgation of President Orders 88 of 1972 (Called Second Amendment Order), 136 of 1972 and 24 of 1973, on an application by the transferor claiming that the transaction was an usfructuory mortgage in case 2 of 1973 the local Circle Officer (Revenue) on 24.11.1973 granted redemption and directed the transferee to deliver possession of the land to the transferor in view of the provision Section 95A (4) (6) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy (which shall hereinafter the called the Act) as amended by the said President Orders. 

 3. To my mind question involves in this matter in dispute is whether the transaction is a complete usufractury mortgage as contemplated under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (Act XXVIII of 1951) as amended by President Orders 88 and 136 of 1972 and if so whether the transaction in question is a past and closed one and whether if can be declared as redeemed, as prayed for by plaintiff-petitioner or whether it can be redeemed by a separate suit within 60 years. "Complete usufractuory mortgage" has been defined in Section 2, Sub-section 6 of the Act as follows:- 

 4. In Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885, Section 260 was inserted by amending Act IV of 1928 which came into force on 22.2.29 with object to protect a Raiyat so that no Mahazan could keep a raiyat out of his land for more than 15 years on the plea of non-payment of petty loan. The amending Act IV of 1928 of Bengal Tenancy Act introduced a new definition of Complete usufractuary mortgage by section 3(3) of the the Bengal Tenancy Act. Definition of complete usufractuary mortgage, is same both in Bengal Tenancy Act and in State Acquisition and Tenancy Act which has been quoted above. Said 15 years was reduced to 7 years by Ordinance No. XXI of 1969. 

 5. Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act after amendment by President Orders 88 and 136 of 1972, stands as follows:- 

 "Para 5. But on perusual of the judgment of the High Court Division it is found that learned Advocate of both the parties who appeared there were confused between the period of subsistence of a usufructuary mortgage and the period of limitation in the case of a suit for redemption of a mortgaged land. The maximum period for which a usufructuary mortgage can be entered into was fifteen years under section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, but by ordinance No. XXI of 1969 section 95 was amended and thereby the maximum period for usufructuary mortgage was reduced to seven years. And unless earlier redeemed by repayment of the consideration a mortgager acquires right to redemption on the expiry of the maximum period of seven yeas, and if the mortgage does not voluntarily restore possession of the land to the corgagor, the latter may file a suit for redemption within a period of 60  wars from the date of accrual of his right of redemption. In this case the suit of redemption and as such it is not barred by limitation."
